metadata.summary: Manchester City have agreed a £65m deal with Everton for winger Iliman Ndiaye as an alternative to Cody Gakpo.
metadata.content: Iliman Ndiaye transfer news: Man City agree £65m deal for Everton winger as Tottenham turn attention to Mykhailo Mudryk | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Iliman Ndiaye transfer news: Man City agree £65m deal for Everton winger as Tottenham turn attention to Mykhailo Mudryk Manchester City advancing in talks with Everton to sign winger Iliman Ndiaye; City had £80m bid for Liverpool's Cody Gakpo rejected on Monday; Spurs had been in talks over Ndiaye and have turned attention to Chelsea's Mykhailo Mudryk By Gianluca Di Marzio, Lyall Thomas, Vinny O'Connor, Michael Bridge and Kaveh Solhekol Monday 31 August 2026 20:24, UK Manchester City have agreed a £65m deal with Everton for winger Iliman Ndiaye as an alternative to Cody Gakpo. With contact already established between City and Everton over Jack Grealish, discussions have moved swiftly. City's deal is broken up into a £60m guaranteed payment plus £5m in bonuses. Richarlison's reluctance to make a final decision on a move to Everton held up Spurs' advanced talks involving Ndiaye that had been ongoing since yesterday. metadata.summary: Derek McInnes' immediate touchline ban has been reduced following Rangers' appeal.
metadata.content: Derek McInnes: Rangers manager's touchline ban changed after appeal over 'disgusting' comment last season | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Breaking Derek McInnes: Rangers manager's touchline ban changed after appeal over 'disgusting' comment last season Rangers appealed the four-match ban handed to Derek McInnes; former Hearts boss described the awarding of a penalty to Celtic at Motherwell as "disgusting"; McInnes will now serve an immediate two-match touchline ban instead of three after appeal hearing Monday 31 August 2026 19:02, UK Image: Derek McInnes' immediate touchline ban has been reduced Derek McInnes' immediate touchline ban has been reduced following Rangers' appeal. The 55-year-old was initially handed a four-match suspension by the Scottish FA, with three of those games to be served immediately. While the overall ban remains in place, he will now only serve two of those with immediate effect, while the other two will only be triggered should he breach disciplinary rule 72 again before the end of this season. As part of disciplinary rule 72 you can not: (i) criticise the decision(s) and/or performance(s) of any or all match official(s) in such a way as to indicate bias or incompetence on the part of such match official; or (ii) make remarks about such match official(s) which impinge on his character Got Sky? messages.text: Is now the right time for Djokovic to retire after 'heart-breaking' US Open loss?

metadata.summary: Novak Djokovic said he "despised" every moment of the five-set, near five-hour ordeal which ended his US Open hopes in the first round, so now the question is whether he calls time on his trophy-laden career.
metadata.content: US Open: Is now the right time for Novak Djokovic to retire after 'heart-breaking' first-round exit in New York? | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content Opinion US Open: Is now the right time for Novak Djokovic to retire after 'heart-breaking' first-round exit in New York? Novak Djokovic will turn 40 next May and after his shock exit in New York there is talk that the former world No 1 should call time on his career; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app By Raz Mirza at Flushing Meadows, New York Monday 31 August 2026 19:08, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gigi Salmon is joined by Tim Henman and Ryan Harrison to debate whether Novak Djokovic should consider retirement after ongoing health issues and a shock first-round exit at the 2026 US Open Novak Djokovic said he "despised" every moment of the five-set, near five-hour ordeal which ended his US Open hopes in the first round, so now the question is whether he calls time on his trophy-laden career. The 24-time Grand Slam champion was knocked out in the first round of the US Open for the first time, beaten by Mariano Navone of Argentina . Djokovic was 19-0 in the US Open first round and hadn't lost his opening match in any major since Paul Goldstein beat him at the Australian Open in 2006. messages.text: Constitution Hill set for serious test at Kempton on Saturday

metadata.summary: Constitution Hill looks likely to face a serious examination of his big-race ambitions on the Flat when he goes for the William Hill September Stakes at Kempton Park on Saturday, with new jockey Billy Loughnane in the saddle.
metadata.content: Constitution Hill set for serious test at Kempton on Saturday | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Constitution Hill set for serious test at Kempton on Saturday The September Stakes is set to pose a very different question of Constitution Hill with top-class rivals Gethin, Bay City Roller and Tornado Alert all set to face Nicky Henderson's star Monday 31 August 2026 18:15, UK Image: Ryan Moore was drafted in to ride Constitution Hill at Kempton in place of the suspended Oisin Murphy Constitution Hill looks likely to face a serious examination of his big-race ambitions on the Flat when he goes for the William Hill September Stakes at Kempton Park on Saturday, with new jockey Billy Loughnane in the saddle. Nicky Henderson's former superstar hurdler is two from two since switching to the level, but the Group Three contest at the Sunbury track represents a major step up. The nine-year-old has been ridden by Oisin Murphy and Ryan Moore so far in his new adventure, but Loughnane's name appeared alongside the Seven Barrows runner for the weekend on the British Horseracing Authority administration site. metadata.summary: Liverpool have rejected an £80m offer from Manchester City for winger Cody Gakpo, with City turning their attention to Everton's Iliman Ndiaye.
metadata.content: Cody Gakpo transfer news: Man City consider options after Liverpool reject £80m bid for winger | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Cody Gakpo transfer news: Man City consider options after Liverpool reject £80m bid for winger Man City consider options after Liverpool reject £80m bid Cody Gakpo; City interested in Everton winger Iliman Ndiaye, who is in advanced talks with Tottenham; City allowed Savio and Omar Marmoush to join Tottenham this month, and Jack Grealish is of interest to Everton and Sunderland Monday 31 August 2026 19:26, UK Liverpool have rejected an £80m offer from Manchester City for winger Cody Gakpo, with City turning their attention to Everton's Iliman Ndiaye . Sky Sports News understands Liverpool were concerned about their chances of bringing in a replacement for the Dutchman. As things stand, they are unwilling to let him leave in this transfer window - which then brought City back into play for Ndiaye. Discussions are moving swiftly after City were knocked back for Gakpo, with Spurs having previously established a fee of £60m with Everton for Ndiaye and contact already established between City and Everton over Jack Grealish. messages.text: 'I'm here now' - Brit Samuel goes from world No 1,871 to US Open second round

metadata.summary: Britain's Toby Samuel has come a long way from the start of 2025 - rising from 1,871 in the world to the US Open second round.
metadata.content: US Open: Britain's Toby Samuel's meteoric rise from world No 1,871 and playing in Guatemala to the US Open second round | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open: Britain's Toby Samuel's meteoric rise from world No 1,871 and playing in Guatemala to the US Open second round Britain's Toby Samuel is into the second round at Flushing Meadows where he takes on Czech 18th seed Jiri Lehecka; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app By Raz Mirza at Flushing Meadows, New York Monday 31 August 2026 17:50, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player British qualifier Toby Samuel claimed his first Grand Slam main-draw victory with an impressive straight-sets win over Tomas Machac Britain's Toby Samuel has come a long way from the start of 2025 - rising from 1,871 in the world to the US Open second round. Samuel, who came through qualifying to make his main draw debut at Flushing Meadows, needed just an hour and 32 minutes to beat the former world No 20 Tomas Machac and book his place in the second round. The 23-year-old - dubbed the 'Winchester Rifle' due to his powerful serve - hammered down serves of up to 135mph to blow his Czech opponent away.
